# docker.push tags an image and pushes it to a registry, here a minimal one
# built from Go's standard library and run with docker.container, so nothing
# is pulled. A second run pushes nothing, a new image pushes again, and
# --clean removes the local tag.
[!docker] skip
[!exec:go] skip
[!exec:curl] skip

# HOME is empty, so the docker CLI finds no user-installed buildx plugin.
exec sh -c 'p=$(command -v docker-buildx) || exit 0; mkdir -p "$HOME/.docker/cli-plugins" && ln -s "$p" "$HOME/.docker/cli-plugins/docker-buildx"'

# TEMPORARY: time Go's first use and compile apart from the first bit run.
exec go version
exec go build -o /dev/null ./registry

bit
stdout 'registry ✔ ok'
stdout 'push ▶ docker tag bit-test-payload-[0-9a-f]{12}:[0-9a-f]{64} localhost:[0-9]+/bit-test-payload-[0-9a-f]{12}:v1 && docker push localhost:[0-9]+/bit-test-payload-[0-9a-f]{12}:v1$'
stdout 'push ✔ ok'
bit names
grep '^ref=localhost:[0-9]+/bit-test-payload-[0-9a-f]{12}:v1$' names.sh
exec sh pushed.sh
cp stdout first.txt

bit
stdout 'push · no changes'

# A new image pushes again.
cp changed.txt payload/payload.txt
bit
stdout 'payload ✔ ok'
stdout 'push ▶ .*\(image changed\)'
stdout 'push ✔ ok'
exec sh pushed.sh
! cmp stdout first.txt

cp names.sh saved.sh
bit --clean
stdout 'push ▶ docker rmi localhost:[0-9]+/bit-test-payload-[0-9a-f]{12}:v1'
! exec sh -c '. ./saved.sh && docker image inspect "$ref"'
! exec sh -c '. ./saved.sh && docker container inspect "$registry"'
# docker push records the pushed digest as a name of the image. Neither the
# image pushed first nor the last is left under it.
exec sh -c '. ./saved.sh && docker images -a -q --filter "label=id=$id"'
! stdout .

-- BUILD.bit --
let id   = replace(sha256(project_dir()), "^(.{12}).*$", "$1")
let port = trim(exec("echo $(( 0x#{replace(id, "^(.{4}).*$", "$1")} % 20000 + 30000 ))"))
let arch = replace(replace(trim(exec("docker info --format '{{.Architecture}}'")), "^aarch64$", "arm64"), "^x86_64$", "amd64")

server = go.exe {
  package = "./registry"
  output  = "registry/registry"
  cgo     = false
  goos    = "linux"
  goarch  = arch
}

registry-image = docker.image {
  tag        = "bit-test-registry-#{id}:v1"
  context    = "registry"
  build_args = { ID = id }
  depends_on = [server]
}

registry = docker.container {
  image       = registry-image.ref
  name        = "bit-test-registry-#{id}"
  ports       = ["127.0.0.1:#{port}:5000"]
  healthcheck = { test = "check", interval = 200ms }
}

payload = docker.image {
  tag        = "bit-test-payload-#{id}:v1"
  context    = "payload"
  dockerfile = "../payload.Dockerfile"
  build_args = { ID = id }
}

push = docker.push {
  image      = payload.ref
  tag        = "localhost:#{port}/bit-test-payload-#{id}:v1"
  depends_on = [registry]
}

explicit names = exec {
  command = "printf 'id=%s\nport=%s\nregistry=%s\nref=%s\n' #{id} #{port} bit-test-registry-#{id} #{push.ref} > names.sh"
  outputs = "names.sh"
  inputs  = []
}
-- pushed.sh --
# Check that the registry serves the manifest docker recorded pushing for the
# tag, and print its digest.
. ./names.sh
pushed=$(docker image inspect --format '{{range .RepoDigests}}{{println .}}{{end}}' "$ref" | grep "^localhost:$port/" | sed 's/.*@//')
served=$(curl -fsSI -H 'Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json, application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json, application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json' "http://127.0.0.1:$port/v2/bit-test-payload-$id/manifests/v1" | tr -d '\r' | sed -n 's/^[Dd]ocker-[Cc]ontent-[Dd]igest: //p')
[ -n "$pushed" ] && [ "$pushed" = "$served" ] || { echo "pushed $pushed, served $served" >&2; exit 1; }
echo "$pushed"
-- payload.Dockerfile --
FROM scratch
# A label unique to the project gives its image an ID no other run shares.
ARG ID
LABEL id=$ID
COPY payload.txt /payload.txt
-- payload/payload.txt --
payload
-- changed.txt --
changed
-- registry/Dockerfile --
FROM scratch
ARG ID
LABEL id=$ID
COPY registry /registry
# Docker runs a healthcheck with /bin/sh -c, and scratch has no shell.
COPY registry /bin/sh
ENTRYPOINT ["/registry"]
-- go.mod --
module example.com/registry

go 1.22
-- registry/main.go --
// A registry that keeps pushed blobs and manifests in memory: just enough
// of the distribution API for docker push and a manifest fetch.
package main

import (
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"sync"
)

var (
	uploadPath   = regexp.MustCompile(`^/v2/(.+)/blobs/uploads/([^/]*)$`)
	blobPath     = regexp.MustCompile(`^/v2/(.+)/blobs/(sha256:[0-9a-f]{64})$`)
	manifestPath = regexp.MustCompile(`^/v2/(.+)/manifests/([^/]+)$`)
)

type manifest struct {
	mediaType string
	body      []byte
	digest    string
}

type registry struct {
	mu        sync.Mutex
	blobs     map[string][]byte
	uploads   map[string][]byte
	manifests map[string]manifest
}

func digestOf(body []byte) string {
	sum := sha256.Sum256(body)
	return "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
}

func (reg *registry) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	reg.mu.Lock()
	defer reg.mu.Unlock()
	w.Header().Set("Docker-Distribution-API-Version", "registry/2.0")
	body, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
	if r.URL.Path == "/v2/" {
		return
	}
	if m := uploadPath.FindStringSubmatch(r.URL.Path); m != nil {
		name, id := m[1], m[2]
		if r.Method == http.MethodPost {
			buf := make([]byte, 16)
			rand.Read(buf)
			id = hex.EncodeToString(buf)
		}
		data := append(reg.uploads[id], body...)
		if digest := r.URL.Query().Get("digest"); digest != "" {
			delete(reg.uploads, id)
			reg.blobs[digest] = data
			w.Header().Set("Location", "/v2/"+name+"/blobs/"+digest)
			w.Header().Set("Docker-Content-Digest", digest)
			w.WriteHeader(http.StatusCreated)
			return
		}
		reg.uploads[id] = data
		w.Header().Set("Location", "/v2/"+name+"/blobs/uploads/"+id)
		w.Header().Set("Docker-Upload-UUID", id)
		w.Header().Set("Range", fmt.Sprintf("0-%d", max(len(data)-1, 0)))
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusAccepted)
		return
	}
	if m := blobPath.FindStringSubmatch(r.URL.Path); m != nil {
		blob, ok := reg.blobs[m[2]]
		if !ok {
			http.Error(w, `{"errors":[{"code":"BLOB_UNKNOWN"}]}`, http.StatusNotFound)
			return
		}
		w.Header().Set("Docker-Content-Digest", m[2])
		w.Header().Set("Content-Length", strconv.Itoa(len(blob)))
		if r.Method == http.MethodGet {
			w.Write(blob)
		}
		return
	}
	if m := manifestPath.FindStringSubmatch(r.URL.Path); m != nil {
		name, ref := m[1], m[2]
		if r.Method == http.MethodPut {
			man := manifest{r.Header.Get("Content-Type"), body, digestOf(body)}
			reg.manifests[name+":"+ref] = man
			reg.manifests[name+"@"+man.digest] = man
			w.Header().Set("Location", "/v2/"+name+"/manifests/"+man.digest)
			w.Header().Set("Docker-Content-Digest", man.digest)
			w.WriteHeader(http.StatusCreated)
			return
		}
		man, ok := reg.manifests[name+":"+ref]
		if !ok {
			man, ok = reg.manifests[name+"@"+ref]
		}
		if !ok {
			http.Error(w, `{"errors":[{"code":"MANIFEST_UNKNOWN"}]}`, http.StatusNotFound)
			return
		}
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", man.mediaType)
		w.Header().Set("Docker-Content-Digest", man.digest)
		w.Header().Set("Content-Length", strconv.Itoa(len(man.body)))
		if r.Method == http.MethodGet {
			w.Write(man.body)
		}
		return
	}
	http.NotFound(w, r)
}

func main() {
	// As /bin/sh -c, run the healthcheck: is the registry answering?
	if filepath.Base(os.Args[0]) == "sh" {
		if resp, err := http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:5000/v2/"); err == nil && resp.StatusCode == http.StatusOK {
			os.Exit(0)
		}
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	reg := &registry{
		blobs:     map[string][]byte{},
		uploads:   map[string][]byte{},
		manifests: map[string]manifest{},
	}
	if err := http.ListenAndServe(":5000", reg); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}
